summary.title: Checklist: what had to be done before deploying microservices to production
summary.one_liner: A checklist of production-readiness criteria for microservices, covering logging, monitoring, alerting, configuration, graceful shutdown, queue handling and deployment automation.
keywords: max tasks per instance restart memory leak
takeaways: Every microservice should have a README description, monitoring metrics, and configured alerts before going to production
Logs should go to STDOUT/STDERR in JSON with agreed fields and a LOG_LEVEL environment variable
Services need liveness and readiness probes, graceful SIGTERM handling, and regular database connection checks
Queue consumers should use retries and dead letter queues, and non-scalable services must be clearly documented
Deployment must be fully automated through CI/CD, with configuration from environment variables and resource limits kept outside the git repo
summary.summary: The author, drawing on experience fighting production incidents, presents a checklist of criteria a microservice should meet before being deployed to production. The items cover documentation (README, runbooks), observability (metrics, alerts, JSON logs to STDOUT, log levels), operational behaviour (liveness/readiness probes, graceful shutdown, DB reconnection, dead letter queues, horizontal scaling, self-restart after a message limit), and delivery concerns (locked dependencies, Docker, environment configuration, resource limits, automated CI/CD, identifiable User-agent, licensing and unsupported libraries). Examples are drawn from real incidents with Kubernetes, RabbitMQ, Logstash and Kafka consumers, and the author invites readers to extend the list.
